reference: bench-src/ref/gen_lifttraffic.py — up-peak RTT with S and H as expectations by enumeration (cross-checked against the equal-population closed forms), Peters closed-form jerk-limited flight times, criteria restated, brute-force sizing grid and zoning over every contiguous split and every car allocation
reference_citations: CIBSE Guide D 2025 ch. 3 official up-peak calculation spreadsheet (cibse-guide-4-2025-uppeak-calculation.xlsx, sheet Input and Results; Fig. 3.4 Example 2): published worked example N 14, P 8.064 / 7.064 (S, H, t_s, RTT, INT, HC5, %POP)
CIBSE Guide D: Transportation systems in buildings, 2020, ch. 4 (up-peak round-trip time, interval, handling capacity, average waiting time relation)
G. Barney, L. Al-Sharif: Elevator Traffic Handbook — Theory and Practice, 2nd ed., Routledge 2016 (S and H for unequal floor populations)
ISO 8100-32:2020 Planning and selection of passenger lifts
EN 81-20:2020 5.4.2 (number of passengers = rated load / 75 kg)
R. D. Peters: Ideal lift kinematics, Elevator Technology 6, IAEE 1996
tolerance: published worked examples within relative 0.5 % of the printed (rounded) numbers; all other quantities within relative 1e-9 (both sides analytic); AWT range flag, verdicts, sizing best option, feasible count, zoning split and car allocation exact; preset buildings must equal the restated ones
restated_conventions: Restated from the tool, not independent (CR-16): the criteria table per building use and the AWT light rule, the up-peak geometry (main terminal, zone, interfloor height, express run; D-VT-13), the sizing grid with its sort order and the hospital minimum load, the zoning ranking key. Independent: the S/H/RTT/INT/HC5/AWT/ATT formulas and the flight times, which are also checked against published worked examples.
scope: In the loaded page: VTCore.upPeak on the published worked examples, VTTraffic.analyse / sizing / zoning for the 9 groups of the 8 shared preset buildings, VTCore.upPeak on 180 synthetic cases (N 5/12/25, equal and rising populations, 3 drives, 2 floor heights with and without express run, 5 cars/loads/load factors 0.4–0.9 covering every AWT branch; ATT, AJT and the AWT range flag compared) and VTCore.motion flight time and peak speed on 54 kinematic cases. Not covered: the UI, the scenario bar, CSV/JSON export (checked by _vt/traffic/browser.mjs).
